claims.claim_text: A git commit records a full snapshot of the tracked tree, not a diff, plus the object names of its parent commit(s).
claims.evidence_needed: official documentation of the commit object format
claims.source: Git documentation, 'Git Internals - Git Objects' and gitrepository-layout(5), git-scm.com, and Pro Git 2nd ed. ch. 10.2
claims.caveats: Storage is deduplicated and packed; 'full snapshot' is the logical model, not the on-disk byte layout.

claims.claim_text: git log -S<string> shows only the commits that change the number of occurrences of <string> in a file.
claims.caveats: Counts occurrences; a change that rewrites the line without changing the count of that substring is not shown (use -G for regex-match-any-change).

claims.claim_text: git log -L <start>,<end>:<file> shows the history of the given line range, following the range across renames and line-number shifts.
claims.caveats: -L implies --patch and cannot be combined with pathspec arguments.

claims.claim_text: git blame annotates each line of a file with the last commit that modified it; blame --reverse walks history forward to find the last commit a line survived into.
claims.caveats: 'Last modified' respects -w / -M / -C options; without them, whitespace-only and move-only changes count as modifications.

claims.claim_text: One reading of why developers avoid these commands is that GUI blame is discoverable and the CLI equivalents are not surfaced in common workflows.
claims.evidence_needed: framed as the author's interpretation, not a measured claim
claims.source: Author's synthesis from teaching three teams; no survey.
claims.caveats: Anecdotal; presented in the book explicitly as 'one explanation', not as fact.

claims.claim_text: When a bug points at a line, run git log -L on that line range before reading the surrounding code.
claims.evidence_needed: flows from C-03; a workflow recommendation, not an evidence claim
claims.caveats: Assumes the line's current content is stable enough to range-select; for heavily churned lines, -S on a distinctive token is faster.
